author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Vietnamese electric-vehicle maker VinFast has appointed Pham Nhat Quan Anh, the 33-year-old eldest son of founder Pham Nhat Vuong, as global chief executive. Quan Anh was already VinFast’s global chairman and chief executive of its Vietnam business. He replaces his father in the worldwide CEO role while remaining chief executive of Vingroup metals unit VinMetal.

The leadership change comes during a broad financial and operating restructuring. VinFast is pursuing an asset-light model that includes transferring about $530 million in manufacturing assets and roughly $6.9 billion in debt to a buyer group. The automaker is also concentrating overseas growth on Southeast Asia and India after an expensive international expansion.

VinFast reported a 42% increase in first-quarter revenue but continued to record net losses and rely heavily on backing from its founder. The company is balancing higher vehicle deliveries with the capital demands of factories, charging networks and new-market entry. Putting a family member with existing operating roles in charge consolidates management as the EV maker tries to turn sales growth into a more durable global business.
dek: Pham Nhat Quan Anh, 33, takes the top role as the Vietnamese EV maker shifts assets and debt while expanding in Asia.
headline: VinFast names founder’s son global CEO amid restructuring
